questions.knowledge_point: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the X-Axis
questions.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}$ is enclosed between the curve $y={x}^{2}$ and the line $y=1$ for $0\le x\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/28a3f0e1eda23169a649276a9cde34d3d96cdd75d5b2bc71c3535604612526e5.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 15{x}^{2}\sqrt{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}15{x}^{2}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}{y}^{3/2}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{2}{5}{y}^{5/2}]}_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}(1-|x{|}^{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{2}-6{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{x}^{8}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =(2-\frac{3}{4})-0 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A thin plate $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{y}$ is enclosed between the curve $y=2-{x}^{2}$ and  the line $y=1$ for $-1\le x\le 1.$ Find the moment of the plate about the $x$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/2d08bcbbcd7ec4d8c388d24728c3f3afdc7c954497f342e9ac2b459fad24e5d2.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,1\le y\le 2-{x}^{2}}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{3}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}3\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2-{x}^{2}}3\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[y]_{y=1}^{y=2-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3[2-{x}^{2}-1]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}3-3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[3x-{x}^{3}]}_{x=-1}^{x=1} \\  & =(3-1)-(-3+1) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{15{x}^{2}}{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}15{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot [y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}\cdot (1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}15{x}^{2}-15{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[5{x}^{3}-3{x}^{5}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.

Therefore, the moment is

$$

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is a type I plane region, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/07701125c6acc36d127556bf95940bf0f74ba9ef3072f3af22dac26edc053a74.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 4x}

and $\lambda (x,y)=x.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4x}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{4x}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot [y]_{y=0}^{y=4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot 4x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}

Therefore, the moment is

$$

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/ddc11fc93f034c3d650854e21f178716c941c18f12eb94123e1af2c835c47981.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{x}}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=2y.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot 2y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}2xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{x}}2y\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot [{y}^{2}]_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x(x-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type I plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=2{e}^{y}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot 2{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{0}2x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x[{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{0}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x\cdot [{e}^{y}]_{y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x}^{y=0}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x(1-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}2x-2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{2}-\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{x=1/2}^{x=1} \\  & =(1-\frac{2}{3})-(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{12}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: The lamina $D={(x,y)\,:\,{y}^{2}\le x\le 1,\,\frac{1}{2}\le y\le 1}$ has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{x}.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{1}{x}.$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{2}}^{1}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}[x]_{x={y}^{2}}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}1-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=1/2}^{y=1} \\  & =(1-\frac{1}{3})-(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{24}) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Find the Center of Mass of a Plane Lamina
questions.problem: Consider a thin plate $D$ that has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}$ and is enclosed between the curve $y={x}^{3}$ and the $x$-axis for $1\le x\le 2.$ Given that the mass of the plate is $2$ units and its center of mass is located at $(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y}),$ what is the value of $\overset{―}{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y})=(\frac{{M}_{y}}{m},\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}),
$$

where 

- $m={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- ${M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A\,$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- ${M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type I plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/b6e8af58b8e7ba5f909d226b895bb39b3fc94e53686e4718eb32c9bb4ee61c08.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}.$ 

Since we require the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $y$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\cdot [y]_{y=0}^{y={x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\cdot {x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{2}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =4-1 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{y}}{m}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Find the Center of Mass of a Plane Lamina
questions.problem: Consider a thin plate $D$ that has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=x+y$ and is enclosed between the curve $x=2y$ and the $y$-axis for $0\le y\le 1.$ Given that the mass of the plate is $\frac{4}{3}$ units and its center of mass is located at $(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y}),$ what is the value of $\overset{―}{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y})=(\frac{{M}_{y}}{m},\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}),
$$

where 

- $m={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- ${M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A\,$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- ${M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/3097e540292efd601743ba8de24acffc3b51469e77561b2bccbd799d1125e1ed.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2y,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)=x+y.$ 

Since we require the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $y$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot (x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}+xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2y}{x}^{2}+xy\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+\frac{{x}^{2}y}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8{y}^{3}}{3}+2{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{14{y}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{7{y}^{4}}{6}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{7}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{y}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{7}{6})}{(\frac{4}{3})}=\frac{7}{8}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Find the Center of Mass of a Plane Lamina
questions.problem: Consider the lamina that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}$ and has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)=4xy.$ Given that the mass of the lamina is $21$ units and its center of mass is located at $(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y}),$ what is the value of $\overset{―}{y}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y})=(\frac{{M}_{y}}{m},\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}),
$$

where 

- $m={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- ${M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A\,$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- ${M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Since we require the $y$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $x$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot 4xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}4x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4x{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{2}}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}4x{[\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y={x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{4{x}^{7}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{8}}{6}]}_{x=1}^{x=2} \\  & =\frac{256}{6}-\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{85}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{y}=\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{85}{2})}{21}=\frac{85}{42}.
$$

Since we require the $y$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $x$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot \frac{1}{xy}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{{e}^{-y}}^{1}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{x={e}^{-y}}^{x=1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}0-(-y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{y}=\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}=\frac{4}{2}=2.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Find the Center of Mass of a Plane Lamina
questions.problem: Consider a thin plate $D$ that has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)={y}^{2}$ and is enclosed between the curve $x=1-{y}^{2}$ and the $y$-axis for $-1\le y\le 1.$ Given that the mass of the plate is $\frac{4}{15}$ units and its center of mass is located at $(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y}),$ what is the value of $\overset{―}{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda (x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overset{―}{x},\overset{―}{y})=(\frac{{M}_{y}}{m},\frac{{M}_{x}}{m}),
$$

where 

- $m={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- ${M}_{x}={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A\,$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- ${M}_{y}={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/78f9da3d48727d2cb3c447be0f4050a044c4aabe29179fd31f04cd7b6c66eabd.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1-{y}^{2},\,-1\le y\le 1}
$$

and $\lambda (x,y)={y}^{2}.$ 

Since we require the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $y$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot {y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1-{y}^{2}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=1-{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot (1-2{y}^{2}+{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{4}+{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}-2{y}^{4}+{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{2}{5}{y}^{5}+\frac{1}{7}{y}^{7}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{5}+\frac{1}{7} \\  & =\frac{8}{105}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{y}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{8}{105})}{(\frac{4}{15})}=\frac{2}{7}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Find the Centroid of a Plane Lamina
questions.problem: Consider the thin plate $D$ enclosed between the curve $x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}$ and the $x$-axis for $-2\le y\le 0.$ Given that the area of the plate is $\pi ,$ find the $x$-coordinate of its centroid.
questions.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area ${A}_{D}$ is given by $({x}_{c},{y}_{c}),$ where

$$
{x}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\,\text{d}A,\,{y}_{c}=\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}y\,\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/14c292e8a224b59c143d0e8a57d43b554ce298cd4f44fc2169f516d683e8c35a.png)

So, we have 

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{4-{y}^{2}},\,-2\le y\le 0}
$$

and ${A}_{D}=\pi .$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{4-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}\frac{4-{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{\int }_{-2}^{0}4-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }{[4y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }[0-(-8+\frac{8}{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\cdot \frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: The Moment of a Plane Lamina About the Y-Axis
canonical_examples.problem: The lamina $D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le y  ,\, 0 \le y \le 1 \big\}$ has the mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y.$ Find the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The moment of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda(x,y) \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

In our case, $D$ is represented as a type II plane region and $\lambda(x,y) = x^2y .$ 

Therefore, the moment is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}x\cdot {x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[{\int }_{0}^{y}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{{y}^{4}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{y}^{5}}{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{6}}{24}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{1}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Find the Center of Mass of a Plane Lamina
canonical_examples.problem: Consider a thin plate $D$ that has the mass density function $\lambda (x,y) = x+y$ and is enclosed between the curve $y=x$ and the $x$-axis for $0 \leq x \leq 1.$ Given that the mass of the plate is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ units and its center of mass is located at $( \overline{x}, \overline{y} ),$ what is the value of $\overline{y}?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a lamina $D$ with the mass density function $\lambda(x,y)$ is given by 

$$
(\overline{x},\overline{y}) = \left( \dfrac{M_y}{m}, \dfrac{M_x}{m} \right),
$$

where 

- $\displaystyle m = \iint \limits_D \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the mass of the lamina,

- $\displaystyle M_x = \iint\limits_D y \, \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $x$-axis, and

- $\displaystyle M_y = \iint\limits_D x \, \lambda (x,y) \: \textrm{d}A$ is the moment of the lamina about the $y$-axis.

Notice that $D$ is a type I plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/b872242423692a20a9d50658c99d9e8cee7c9b2737fb96592bc2bc35b4f72c32.png)

So, we have 

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \:0 \le x \le 1, \: 0 \le y \le x \big\}
$$

and $\lambda(x,y) = x+y.$ 

Since we require the $y$-coordinate of the center of mass, we need to compute the moment about the $x$-axis: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}y\,\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}y\cdot (x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}xy+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}xy+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{6}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{6}{[\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=1} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{24}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\overline{y} = \dfrac{M_x}{m} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{5}{24}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{5}{12}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Find the Centroid of a Plane Lamina
canonical_examples.problem: Consider the thin plate $D$ enclosed between the curve $x=\sqrt{1-y^2}$ and the $y$-axis for $-1 \leq y \leq 1.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of its centroid.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The centroid of a lamina $D$ with area $A_D$ is given by $(x_c, y_c),$ where

$$
\displaystyle x_c = \dfrac{1}{A_D} \iint\limits_D x \, \: \textrm{d}A, \qquad 
\displaystyle y_c = \dfrac{1}{A_D} \iint\limits_D y \, \: \textrm{d}A.
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II plane region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14068268/assets/a7992c54f85f85cab3d9f923b8daca62c410393b364d30bcfbf5cff5efc93bbd.png)

So, we have 

$$
D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \le x \le \sqrt{1-y^2}, \: -1 \le y \le 1 \big\}
$$

and 

$$
A_D = \dfrac12 \cdot \pi\cdot 1^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinate of the centroid is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{c} & =\frac{1}{{A}_{D}}{∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-1}^{1}1-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{[y-\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }[(1-\frac{1}{3})-(-1+\frac{1}{3})] \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot \frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
